image_prompt.text: Flat placement strips flanking both sides of the city pathway where players drop their units
A narrowing in the city street where waves bunch up and area damage pays off
Camera Base at the end of the pathway, standing in for the health pool the player is defending
A big giant building the player spawns inside, with a summoning area off to the left
A miniature city the pathway runs through, the buildings only slightly taller than the player

layout_placement.text: The mouth of the pathway opposite Camera Base where each wave of toilets enters
Camera Base as the objective volume that takes damage when enemies reach it
A teleporter in the spawn building sized for five players, with a start trigger that launches the round immediately

notes: This is really two maps - the spawn building with the summon area and teleporter, then the city battlefield - linked by a teleporter. The dominant genre owns one shape, so the lobby and its separate-map and interior costs are not represented in the route.

The summon rolls, rarities, unit stats and upgrades, cash rewards, inventory, and the ten-wave table are progression and mechanics; only the summon station and the placement strips have a spatial footprint.
The player being slightly smaller than the miniature city buildings is a scale relationship the band cannot express.

answers.ask: How big is the tiny city - one street with the base at the end, or several blocks?
answers.answer: Make it one small city street with the Camera Base on one side of the pathway and the toilets spawning from the other side.

answers.ask: Is the spawn building a separate map you teleport out of, or is it attached to the city?
answers.answer: The big spawn building should be a separate lobby map, and the teleporter takes players into the city match.

answers.ask: The teleporter fits five - is the whole run five players co-operating on one lane?
answers.answer: Yes, up to five players should play together co-operatively on the same lane for all 10 waves.
